title: Auditable day-2 operations and model lifecycle for fleets of DDIL edge clusters (image, model, certificate and policy updates; validate, distribute, roll back and prove what ran where; low-signature observability a signal soldier can act on)
problem: Once containerized C2/ISR software and ATR/CV models are fielded on tens to hundreds of tactical edge nodes, pushing image/model/certificate/policy updates across air-gapped or intermittently connected clusters, validating them locally, tracking which version runs where, rolling back safely and producing continuous-monitoring evidence for the authorization boundary is still done by contractor field support and manual steps, because the enterprise tooling (Big Bang/UDS/Palantir/OpenShift consoles, Prometheus-style observability, eMASS) assumes reachback.

current_workflow: Build and scan images/models in a connected software factory (Platform One Iron Bank/Big Bang, UDS, vendor pipeline, Linchpin-style ML pipeline).
Package into an OCI/Zarf/UDS bundle or vendor-specific data-mesh artifact; models are packaged ad hoc as containers/ONNX with no separate model-evidence record (INFERENCE).
Move the bundle by approved media or cross-domain solution to the target enclave when a link or courier is available; full-size pushes rather than deltas where bandwidth is scarce (INFERENCE).

Vendor field service representatives or contractor support load the local registry and run upgrades node by node; certificates are rotated by hand; version state is confirmed by walking to the node or through vendor dashboards that assume connectivity.
Deployment state and scan/STIG evidence are recorded manually for the ISSM; when links drop, continuous-monitoring feeds stop and cATO/RMF evidence goes stale until reconnection (INFERENCE).
Model drift and version mismatch are discovered anecdotally during exercises (Ivy Sting, Ivy Mass, PC-C6); rollback is manual; retraining data is sent back when bandwidth allows.
current_solution: Air-gap packaging: Zarf/UDS (Defense Unicorns), Big Bang bundles (Platform One), Red Hat OpenShift for DCGS-A (CECOM SEC), Rancher Government (RKE2/Hauler), Spectro Cloud Palette Edge; application-vendor stacks: Palantir Apollo/PFCS Forward for Palantir-hosted apps, Anduril Lattice for Team Anduril NGC2 nodes; MLOps inside team stacks (Striveworks Chariot via Lattice SDK, TurbineOne on-device training); enterprise models via GenAI.mil (IL5 cloud only). Everything between these pieces (fleet-wide version ledger, offline attestation, model validation gate, EMCON-aware telemetry, soldier-executable runbooks) is integrator/FSR labor.
failure: Registries, GitOps control planes, policy servers and certificate authorities become single points of failure when a node is partitioned; there is no vendor-neutral record of which image/model/policy version ran on which node during a partition, so rollback and authorization evidence are reconstructed by hand; observability stacks are chatty and assume uplink; models arriving at a node have no independent local validation gate; and the DoD CIO's own March 2025 study says authorizing officials are biased to caution and reciprocity is lacking, so stale evidence translates directly into fielding delay. NOTE: no primary government document found in this study describes this day-2 failure explicitly; the failure statement is an INFERENCE from architecture, exercise reports and vendor positioning (confidence MEDIUM).

why_existing_startups_havent_solved: Three structural reasons. (1) The high-evidence half of the gap (getting signed bundles into air-gapped clusters) has been commoditized by open source (Zarf, Big Bang) and is the explicit mission of a $136M-funded specialist (Defense Unicorns) and of platform vendors (Red Hat, Rancher Government, Spectro Cloud), so a newcomer has no packaging wedge. (2) The low-evidence half (fleet-wide 'what ran where' attestation, offline continuous-monitoring evidence, model validation gates, EMCON-aware observability, soldier-executable runbooks) requires hands-on access to tactical kits, DoD PKI and CUI/Secret enclaves, which means cleared U.S.-person engineers embedded with units - the exact resource pre-seed startups lack; every startup that has this access (Defense Unicorns, Striveworks, TurbineOne, Second Front) is inside a prime's team or a platform contract and treats day-2 as a service line. (3) The buyer has historically purchased day-2 operations as contractor field-support labor, not as a product, and AOs biased to caution (DoD CIO, Mar 2025) do not yet accept machine-generated offline evidence as a substitute for a human ISSM's records, so there is no demonstrated willingness to pay for the attestation layer.
technical_wedge: A vendor-neutral 'edge fleet ledger' agent for any CNCF cluster (K3s/RKE2/UDS Core/Big Bang/OpenShift): (a) signed, offline-verifiable deployment manifests recording image, model, certificate and policy versions per node with a hash-chained local log; (b) delta-based, resumable artifact sync over any transport including sneakernet media and sub-kilobit links, with content-addressed OCI artifacts so models are first-class versioned objects with attached evaluation/provenance evidence (OpenSSF/Sigstore-style signatures, SBOM, model cards); (c) a local validation gate that runs a canary evaluation of an arriving model against a node-held test set before promotion, with one-command rollback; (d) telemetry-budgeted, store-and-forward observability with EMCON modes and soldier-facing runbooks; (e) reconciliation of the accumulated evidence into eMASS/OSCAL-style continuous-monitoring records when a link returns. The wedge is the evidence and lifecycle layer, not the packaging.

mvp.what: Open-source agent plus a small fleet console demonstrated across five simulated air-gapped K3s/RKE2 clusters on commodity mini-PCs running Big Bang or UDS Core, with open-weight CV models packaged as OCI artifacts; sync exercised over throttled links (8-64 kbit/s) and USB media; evidence exported as OSCAL assessment results.
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Fleet view that stays correct through partitions; model update with local canary evaluation and rollback; certificate/policy rotation replayed offline; 90%+ reduction in telemetry bytes versus stock Prometheus remote-write at equal fault-detection on a scripted fault set; reconciled OSCAL evidence bundle after reconnection.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: That an ISSM-grade record of 'what ran where' can be produced with zero reachback and reconciled without human re-entry; that model updates can be validated and rolled back at the node without an MLOps stack; and that a signal soldier can execute remediation from the console without SRE skills (usability test with veterans).

data_requirement.what: For the MVP: none sensitive - synthetic workloads, open-weight models, public imagery datasets for canary evaluation, synthetic fault and link-outage scripts. For a credible military demo: a unit's actual edge stack composition, STIG/scan outputs, node logs from an exercise and the system security plan (all CUI), plus DoD PKI test certificates.
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: MVP data is fully obtainable. CUI-level artifacts require a sponsoring program office or prime team and a U.S.-person engineer under a CRADA, SBIR/OT data-rights clause or subcontract; the non-U.S. founder cannot handle CUI/ITAR technical data without authorization (counsel). Real NGC2 node configurations are inside prime-owned prototypes and are not publicly available.

entry_vehicle.eligibility_notes: SBIR/STTR requires the firm to be >50% owned and controlled by U.S. citizens or permanent residents (or by other eligible U.S. small businesses); an Indonesian founder who is not a U.S. person, holding a large equity stake, can make the company ineligible unless the cap table is structured so U.S.-person ownership exceeds 50% - requires counsel before any SBIR submission. OT/CSO awards (DIU, AFWERX) carry no per-se citizenship rule, but CUI handling (NIST 800-171/CMMC Level 2), DoD PKI, ITAR technical data (if models/sensors are defense articles) and any Secret-level work all restrict what a non-U.S. person may access; FOCI adjudication is triggered by foreign ownership/control, not by a foreign employee alone. Describe constraints; get counsel.

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: Yes, within 6-18 months for their own stacks: Palantir Apollo already does versioned rollout/rollback and PFCS Forward covers accredited edge; Anduril controls the NGC2 node fleet and can add attestation to Lattice; Defense Unicorns can add fleet attestation to UDS and is funded to do so; Red Hat ACM and Rancher Fleet already do connected-fleet management. L3Harris is less likely (hardware/radio focus).
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: A startup wins only in the vendor-neutral seam: an ISSM-facing evidence layer that spans Anduril, Palantir, OpenShift and UDS nodes because no single vendor is trusted to attest the others, plus model-as-artifact validation that program AI leads (Linchpin, CDAO) want independent of the app vendor. That seam is real but narrow, and the government may fill it itself (CDAO AI-assurance guidance, Platform One). Honest verdict: REJECT as a standalone company unless the team can secure (a) a cleared U.S.-person engineer embedded with an NGC2 unit or PM C2 Infrastructure and (b) a platform-owner partnership within 12 months; otherwise this is a feature Defense Unicorns or Palantir ships first.

regulatory_burden.explanation: Pure software and open-source core keep the MVP unregulated, but a credible product must handle CUI (NIST SP 800-171 / CMMC Level 2), integrate DoD PKI, potentially process ITAR-controlled technical data if the models/sensors it manages are defense articles, and eventually run inside Secret enclaves (facility clearance via a sponsor). Accreditation of the agent itself (Iron Bank hardening, STIG compliance, possibly a cATO inheritance package) is a certification burden that is smaller than a CDS but real. Not legal advice; ITAR/EAR classification of the product and any FOCI exposure need counsel.
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: The Indonesian founder (not assumed a U.S. person) cannot hold a U.S. security clearance, should not access CUI/ITAR technical data without authorization, and a large foreign-national equity stake can (a) defeat SBIR ownership eligibility and (b) raise FOCI questions if a facility clearance is later needed. Workable mitigations to explore with counsel: keep the open-source core and commercial/dual-use business as the non-U.S. founder's domain, keep U.S.-person ownership above SBIR thresholds, and put all CUI/classified work behind a U.S.-person engineer and access controls. The German founder's expected permanent residency helps for SBIR ownership counting but clearance eligibility generally requires citizenship.

dual_use_potential.explanation: Fleet lifecycle, offline attestation and bandwidth-budgeted observability for air-gapped/edge Kubernetes have direct analogs in maritime, mining, energy/OT, retail and satellite ground segments; the commercial market is, however, already served by Spectro Cloud, Rancher, Red Hat ACM, Zededa, Chainguard-style supply-chain tools and hyperscaler edge products, so the dual-use path is a crowded commercial infrastructure market rather than an open one. The model-validation-gate and evidence-reconciliation features are the most transferable to regulated industries (medical devices, critical infrastructure).

defensibility.explanation: The packaging and sync primitives are open source and commoditized; durable value would come from being the evidence format an authorizing official accepts (accreditation), being pre-integrated with UDS/Big Bang/Lattice/Apollo (integrations), being installed on a division's node fleet (footprint) and encoding soldier runbooks that units train on (workflow). None of these exists at founding, and all are also available to the incumbents who own the platforms.

why_now: Four changes since 2023: (1) programs re-platformed onto edge Kubernetes (DCGS-A on OpenShift 2025; NGC2 hub/spoke compute at 65+ nodes by 2026; Klas/Anduril Voyager kits), creating fleets where none existed; (2) DoD CIO's CSRMC tenets (Sep 2025) replaced RMF's snapshot model with continuous monitoring, automation and ATO revocation, which cannot be satisfied from partitioned nodes with today's tooling; (3) edge AI moved from slideware to procurement (TurbineOne IDIQ Sep 2025, AIDP 72-hour autonomous node requirement Jul 2026, GenAI.mil Dec 2025 with no edge tier), so models are now fielded artifacts needing lifecycle control; (4) PEO C3N's Dec 2025 reorganization created PM C2 Infrastructure as an accountable owner of edge compute, and JWCC UCM's June 2026 draft PWS expands edge computing, so a buyer with a budget line for edge infrastructure now exists.
killer_risk: The pain is real but the buyer already has a funded answer for the evidenced half (Defense Unicorns' $136M-backed UDS/Zarf, Palantir Apollo/PFCS Forward, Red Hat/Rancher) and buys the unevidenced half (fleet attestation, model rollback, soldier observability) as contractor field-support labor inside prime OTAs; no RFI, GAO finding or exercise report names fleet-scale day-2 tooling as a shortfall, so a pre-seed team with one non-U.S. founder and no cleared engineer would be building a feature for platforms it cannot access, in a seam the platform owners can close in one release cycle.
